definitions.meaning: A counting word for 6.02 × 10²³ particles, just as a dozen is a counting word for 12 items. Chemists weigh moles instead of counting particles one by one.
The mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole (g/mol). Carbon-12 is 12 g/mol, hydrogen is 1 g/mol and oxygen is 16 g/mol.
The number of particles in one mole: 6.02 × 10²³. Every mole of any substance contains this many particles.
How heavy a sample is, in grams. Mass links to moles through mass = moles x molar mass, or n = m / M.
A single atom, molecule or ion being counted. A mole counts particles without saying which kind - the kind decides the molar mass.
The ratio of moles in a balanced equation, such as 2 : 1 : 2 for 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O. It scales as a whole when amounts change.

mechanismSteps: A mole is a counting word - one dozen is 12 eggs and one mole is 6.02 × 10²³ particles, far too many to count one by one, so we weigh moles instead of counting them.
Mass to moles - the mass of one mole of carbon-12 is 12 g, its molar mass, so weighing 12 g of carbon gives exactly one mole with n = m / M.
Mole ratios - balanced equations count moles, not grams: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O gives the fixed 2 : 1 : 2 ratio, and doubling one reactant doubles the others.
A common mistake: one mole of everything weighs the same - one mole always has the same number of particles but a different mass, because each substance has its own molar mass.
objectives: Explain what a mole means: a counting word for 6.02 × 10²³ particles
Use n = m / M and mass = moles x molar mass to convert between mass and moles
Use mole ratios from balanced equations, and explain why one mole of different substances has different masses
subject: science
title: The mole: counting atoms by weighing

trap.explanation: The slip: A mole feels like a fixed bag of the same size, so every mole feels equally heavy. The fix: Mass = moles x molar mass: one mole of hydrogen is 1 g but one mole of oxygen is 16 g. A mole fixes the count of particles - the molar mass decides how heavy that count is.
trap.misconception: One mole of anything weighs the same.

workedExample: Trace the mole from counting word to calculation. Step 1 (s1): a mole is a counting word - 1 mole = 6.02 × 10²³ particles, like 1 dozen = 12, so we weigh instead of counting. Step 2 (s2): use n = m / M for carbon: 12 g of carbon divided by its molar mass 12 g/mol gives n = 12 / 12 = 1 mol, written as 12g carbon/12g-per-mol=1 mol. Step 3 (s3): use the mole ratio in 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O, which is 2 : 1 : 2 - so 4 mol of hydrogen needs 2 mol of oxygen and makes 4 mol of water. Step 4 (s4): check the mass each time with mass = moles x molar mass, because one mole of hydrogen is 1 g but one mole of oxygen is 16 g.
